# Silicyte

> Silicyte runs pre-registered, compute-matched tests of whether AI self-improvement actually
> compounds, and publishes the result either way, including nulls. Earlier work on agent guardrail
> uptime and on computational molecule-design evaluation stays published here. Founded October
> 2026. Solo and unincorporated, with $0 revenue and 0 customers; paid services are paused.
> Contact hello@silicyte.com.

**Current focus**: recursive self-improvement, measured. The registered test is Silicyte Ratchet
(silicyte-0119), registered 2026-11-04 16:46 ET, before any model call; pre-registration commit cc5fb5b
(16:47 ET). Question: does a library of verified Python helpers that keeps growing solve more of 400
sealed ARC-AGI-1 evaluation tasks than the same library frozen after round 1, the same tokens spent in one
round, verified exemplars, a matched sham library, and plain extra sampling, all at equal total tokens?
Arms: STOCK, STATIC, ONE-SHOT, EXEMPLAR, SHAM, FLAT-TTC, plus planted positive controls PLANT-DRIP and
PLANT-L1. The sealed id list has sha256 911bf838d8843606d5fc1ba0550a0c23670027bf8f6e32e4e4fbf93854957ddd.
Registered prediction: +2 of 400 (80% band [-8, +14]; calibrated band [-10.68, +17.216]),
P(COMPOUNDS) 0.15. Result: pending. It will be published whatever it shows, including a null.
Page: https://silicyte.com/ratchet. Pre-registration:
https://github.com/braxtonmensah/ratchet/blob/main/PREREG.md. Not arXiv 2605.22148.

**Earlier work, with its correction**: on one laptop fleet a guardrail hook was absent on 29.8% of the
103,850 calls it existed to check; on clean public runners the same load gave 0.0000 absence at a 15 s
budget in every cell up to 24 agents, so the effect belongs to that laptop. See /refusal-uptime and
https://github.com/braxtonmensah/refusal-uptime/tree/loadtest-results.

The earlier research's distinguishing claim follows.

Silicyte's distinguishing claim, with the measurement behind it: in a closed-loop molecular design
system, **deliberately degrading the scoring model made the reported improvement 2.4 times larger**
(+1.3182 against +0.5421, difference -0.7761, standard error 0.0531, t = -14.60, n = 3 seeds per
rung, all six paired shuffled controls inside their pre-registered band). So on this system the
reported gain is not a monotone measure of scorer accuracy. The mechanism of the inversion is
not established.

## Headline measurements, all reproducible

- **Scorer-exploitation intervention**: withholding 80% of the scoring model's training families
  while leaving the evaluation model untouched increased the reported gain 2.4x. t = -14.60.
- **Leakage in Silicyte's own pipeline, found and published**: a cross-validation splitter
  documented as single-linkage clustering was performing greedy first-match assignment. 20.1% of
  held-out MIC rows and 24.6% of HC50 rows had a cross-fold near-twin above 0.80 Levenshtein
  identity, while the usual test that families never span a fold passed 826 of 826. Rebuilt folds
  measure 0.0000 on the same quantity. Score inflation on the safety endpoint was +0.065.
- **Leakage measured in six third-party published splits** (see /benchmark-leakage.html):
  LRGB Peptides-func 65.29%, AMPlify positives 63.47%, PepBenchmark default hybrid split 29.97%
  (E. coli MIC) and 48.56% (haemolysis HC50), AMP Scanner v2 positives 16.71%, AMP Scanner v2
  negatives 0.00%, FLIP meltome 0.29%.
- **The actionable comparison**: PepBenchmark clusters at 30% identity and leaves 29.97% to 48.56%.
  FLIP meltome clusters at 20% identity and assigns whole clusters, and leaves 0.29%. Both cluster
  then split; they land two orders of magnitude apart.
- **Resolution floor**: a gain read off k kept molecules carries an irreducible floor of
  sd*sqrt(2/k). With sd 0.4562 per molecule, that is 0.0645 predicted against 0.0570 measured at
  k = 100.
- **Label reliability** of pooled antimicrobial peptide activity: split-half Spearman 0.7877
  (sd 0.0067), Spearman-Brown corrected 0.8812, implied ceiling 0.9387 **against the pooled label**.
  74.2% of resolvable variance is between organisms; between-organism Spearman median 0.596 over
  491 pairs; within-organism ceilings 0.9590 to 0.9815.

- [Refusal uptime](https://silicyte.com/refusal-uptime): earlier work, measured on one laptop. One
  guardrail was absent on 29.8% of the 103,850 calls it existed to check there; on clean public runners the
  same load gave 0.0000 at a 15 s budget in every cell up to 24 agents, so the effect belongs to that laptop.
  On the laptop, absence rose from 0.2% with one agent running to 53.1% with 11 or more. Presence, coverage, independence and
  override, with the prediction that was wrong, the measured cause (process start-up), and the
  fix (absent on 0 of 2,211 calls at lighter load and 5 of 8,055 at 11 or more agents after it). Not peer reviewed.
- [Benchmark leakage](https://silicyte.com/benchmark-leakage): measured train/test sequence
  overlap in six published peptide and protein machine-learning splits, with the two clean controls
  that validate the instrument.

  DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23441786.
  [PDF](https://silicyte.com/papers/Mensah_DesignLoops_preprint.pdf)

  evaluation table. No account, no upload; the file is processed locally in the browser.

## Code and evidence

- Refusal uptime probe: https://github.com/braxtonmensah/refusal-uptime (release v0.1.0, MIT;
  standard-library Python; computes each Claude Code hook's refusal uptime from your own
  transcripts, locally; includes a canary wrapper and the technical note with every number).

- Evidence archive: https://github.com/braxtonmensah/silicyte-design-loops (release v1.0.0,
  CC BY 4.0). Contains, for every number in the paper, the pre-registration written before the run,
  the instrument that produced it, the result file, and the saved out-of-fold predictions.
- Third-party audit scripts: https://github.com/braxtonmensah/silicyte-design-loops/tree/main/thirdparty
- Archived permanently at Software Heritage: swh:1:snp:7804efeabcc293e1a6b81a3b6d13702d24e14809

## The four diagnostics

1. **LEAK** - does a held-out molecule have a near-twin in training? Measured by transitive
   single-linkage (union-find) clustering at Levenshtein ratio 0.80. Clustering tools in common use
   compare each sequence only to cluster representatives, so transitively similar pairs land in
   different folds and go unnoticed.
2. **FLOOR** - can the reported effect even be seen? A gain read off k kept molecules carries an
   irreducible floor of sd*sqrt(2/k).
3. **TIES** - is the rank statistic tie-corrected? `argsort(argsort(x))` is an ordinal rank and
   biases every correlation when the target has repeated values.
4. **SPLIT** - is the test set actually independent, or did selection touch it?

## How Silicyte states limits

A contamination rate is not an inflation. Silicyte's rates were measured without retraining, and
it does not claim a figure for what leakage is worth on anyone else's reported model. Where it did
retrain, the figure is stated with the model named: its own +0.065 on HC50, and on LRGB
Peptides-func the count ECFP + LightGBM baseline of arXiv 2501.17901 scores +0.1773 macro AP higher
on the shipped split than on corrected splits (sd 0.0094, preregistered gate, rerunnable at
https://github.com/braxtonmensah/peptides-func-split-rerun).

## Free tool: check your own split

- [Split Audit](https://silicyte.com/audit): upload a train/test split and get the exact
  fraction of test rows carrying a training sequence at Levenshtein ratio 0.80 or above. The
  comparison is complete, not sampled, and runs entirely in the visitor's browser, so sequences
  are never uploaded. The leak rate is free. Paid tiers are paused. A contamination rate is not a score
  inflation: no retraining is performed, so it does not say by how much any number is overstated.

## Paid work: paused

Silicyte sells nothing at present. The Model Evaluation Sprint (https://silicyte.com/evaluation), the paid
tiers of the evaluation tool (https://silicyte.com/check), the evals pilot and the expert bench
(https://silicyte.com/careers) are all marked paused, with prices removed. $0 revenue, 0 customers.

- [Checkable biology evals](https://silicyte.com/evals): a free public sample of 4 biology tasks for evaluating AI
  systems (trastuzumab epitope on HER2 from PDB 1N8Z; PTEN variant abundance at 60 held-out positions; Gene Ontology
  enrichment under 13 written conventions; signal peptide cleavage in 100 human proteins). Each task has a key a
  program scores, rebuilt from CC0 or CC BY 4.0 data on every CI run, a deterministic grader, controls that must fail
  (19 of 19 fail) and a reward-hack log (45 of 49 attempts caught; the 4 uncaught are copying the public key). In a
  blind one-shot test a Claude Opus 5.5 agent passed 2 of 4 (the two exact tasks) and failed the two prediction tasks.
  Repository: https://github.com/braxtonmensah/silicyte-bio-evals-sample. The pilot is paused.
  Checkable task data is not new; established data vendors sell verified tasks too.

## Machine-readable measurements

If you need an exact figure with its method and its caveat attached, read the JSON rather than the
prose. Every per-split number on the leakage page is there with its homology control as published,
its exact-overlap rate, its twin rate at Levenshtein ratio 0.80, and its test and train row counts.
It also carries the two measurements that were deliberately excluded from the findings, each with
the reason, so a reader cannot quote them as results by accident.

- [Leakage measurements, JSON](https://silicyte.com/data/leakage-measurements.json): 13 split
  measurements across 5 benchmark families (12 entries; PepBenchmark is read on two datasets),
  plus 2 measured and deliberately excluded with reasons.

Plain-markdown mirrors of every page sit alongside it at the same path with a `.md` extension, for
retrieval without parsing navigation or inline SVG:
